what_its_for: Vemurafenib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of skin cancer called melanoma that has spread to other parts of the body or cannot be removed by surgery. It only works in patients whose cancer has a specific gene change called a BRAF V600 mutation. Your doctor will test for this mutation before starting treatment.
how_to_take: Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, break, or chew the tablets. You can take vemurafenib with or without food, but try to be consistent. Take your doses about 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 960 mg (four 240 mg tablets) taken twice daily, about 12 hours apart. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions, as your dose may be adjusted based on side effects or other factors. Do not change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor or pharmacist.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 4 hours away. If your next dose is less than 4 hours away, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store vemurafenib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect them from heat, light, and moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid prolonged sun exposure while taking vemurafenib, as it can make your skin much more sensitive to sunlight and increase your risk of sunburn and new skin cancers. Wear protective clothing, hats, and sunscreen (SPF 30 or higher) when outdoors. Avoid tanning beds and sunlamps. Tell your doctor about ALL medications you take, including vitamins and herbal supplements, because many medicines can interact with vemurafenib. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel dizzy or have vision problems.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: new skin growths, changes in moles, or sores that do not heal; severe rash, blistering, or skin peeling; joint pain or swelling; eye pain, redness, or vision changes; signs of heart rhythm problems such as fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat, dizziness, or fainting; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; unusual bleeding or bruising; fever, chills, or signs of infection; severe sensitivity to light; or any symptoms that worry you. Also tell your doctor if you are planning to become pregnant or if you think you may be pregnant.
when_it_works: Some patients begin to see results within a few weeks of starting treatment, but it can take longer for others. Your doctor will monitor your response to treatment with regular check-ups and tests. It is important to keep taking this medicine even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Vemurafenib can harm an unborn baby. Both men and women should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 2 weeks after the last dose. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver or kidney problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Tell your doctor about any liver or kidney conditions you have. Elderly patients: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely. Children: Vemurafenib is not approved for use in children under 18 years old.
